# K83-13 · Mathematical notes

## What the pages do

**Generators and a fourfold trace (194).** The writer lists four triples, obtained by leaving out one of the indices 1 to 4. He takes $A$ generated by the displayed families $b,c,t$ and proposes a statement about $B$ as an $A$-module. To look for a missing relation he turns to $\operatorname{Tr}x_1x_2x_3x_4$. The words before this discussion continue a sentence from outside the package.

**Actions and coefficient rings (195).** Crossed calculations involve $\alpha,\beta,\sigma$ and their primed forms. In the curved enclosure he sets three rows of primed letters beside a group action and draws a diagram involving $A,B$, their variants with indices or superscripts, and $\mathbb Z[\Sigma,\Pi]$. The marginal gloss is « Fonctions $G$-invariantes en 3 variables $x,y,z$ ».

**Power traces and integrality (197).** He first writes a power trace as a polynomial in the trace and determinant of $u$, then starts a version for a word in $u,v$. For four factors he treats $x_3x_4$ as one entry. A quadratic in $\tau$ has coefficients indexed by $1,2,(3,4)$. Brackets below the traces and determinants attach names to the coefficients. Two successive ring displays end in a proposed bound of eight over $A$.

**Orderings of four factors (199).** Cyclic reorderings, a shortened reverse row and a cube stand beside two expressions for powers of $\tau$ with coefficients $\alpha$ and $\beta$. A subtraction introduces $\gamma_1$. A separate group diagram and a list of degrees lead into a comparison of $\alpha+\beta\tau$ with the corresponding primed expression. The two-loop leading exponent is doubtful.

**An intermediate ring diagram and a coefficient calculation (200).** The diagram places $A$ and $B$ above objects with group superscripts, including a $B$ between the two columns. The ensuing expansion (input A200) replaces $\tau'$ by $\sigma-\tau$ in a sum of two linear expressions. The final line compares their constant parts and ends « OK ».

**Face traces and edge coefficients (201).** The face quantities on either side of an edge are paired by their sum and product. The author compares two unordered pairs of roots, considers two possible matches and rearranges differences of edge sums. Three cube sketches distinguish orientations, parallel edges and corresponding coefficient labels. The prose then asserts that only three values of each edge coefficient occur.

**Twelve linear relations (203).** A labelled cube fixes opposite primed and unprimed edges and capital vertex labels. Six equations are followed by another six (input A203). The annotation on the last group says that each equation follows from the other five. Beside a second cube he writes a condition for three underlined edge subscripts forming a « demi hexagone ». The sheet ends in a partly written linear combination.

**The vertex and edge dictionary (205).** Vertices $s$, edges $a$ and faces $f$ index separate families. A diagonal through a vertex labels the matrix whose trace and determinant give $b_s,c_s$. Two diagonal indices give the two-factor trace $t_a$. Opposite vertices carry the two orientations of a three-factor trace. Their sum and product are expanded in the lower-order quantities. The long product formula retains a crossed earlier term. A face contributes a cyclic four-factor trace. At the foot, two four-tuples and eight short arrows match the vertices of adjacent faces to matrix indices.

**Edge relations and totals (207).** Two adjacent face traces have a prescribed sum and product. The writer expands the sum as products of traces, then in the indexed generators. For the product he names arguments, including two three-factor traces identified underneath as $T_s,T_t$. The page closes with the counts (input A207) « 28 variables » and « 32 relations ! ».

**The stages of discovery (196, 198, 202, 204 and the typed passage on 200).** L 17 describes how a new idea takes form, with « yin » and « yang » as complementary aspects of discovery. Scan 204 revises that same page in pen. L 18 develops the « conspiration du silence » around this work. L 19 continues the reflection and returns to the purposes of the introduction. L 22 says that attending to the writer's own reservations made them disappear. These are distinct pieces of the typescript.

**Bibliographical and personal footnotes (208).** The notes name two theses, give the writer's account of leaving an editorial board and asking editors to receive his letter, refer to published SGA volumes, and recall the « maison » as an image for mathematical work. The writer describes the letter of 18 February from the perspective of his later correspondence.

## Statements left without proof

- **194.** « je présume que $B$ est fini libre de rang $2^4$ sur $A$ », with « aux seules relations … ci-dessus ». These leaves do not establish freeness or completeness of the proposed relations.
- **197.** « entier sur » the displayed ring and « de degré au plus huit sur $A$ ». The intervening coefficient identifications are written, but a complete derivation of the bound is absent.
- **199.** The side list gives « de degré … sur » several invariant rings and « degré 6 » for the lower diagram. The sheet juxtaposes the claims without a degree argument.
- **201.** « ne dépend que de la direction de $a$ », followed by « il n'y a que trois valeurs » for the two coefficient families. Some associated differences and alternative root identifications are worked out on the same sheet.
- **203.** « $\exists\sigma$ avec » the displayed sum for each « demi hexagone ». A labelled sketch accompanies the assertion.
- **205 and 207.** « on a » introduces trace and coefficient formulas. The expanded product at a vertex is given without a derivation. The corresponding edge product is described through its variables.

## Questions and conjectures

- **194.** « je présume » is the writer's qualification on the rank and freeness claim. « Mais il faudrait trouver la relation » and « peut-être via les $t_{ijk}$ » identify what still has to be found.
- **197.** After « au plus huit », he writes « divisant » beneath the degree statement, between repeat marks. It looks like a trial strengthening of the wording.
- **199.** « de degré $8$ (?) … sur $A$ ». The parenthetical question mark is explicit.
- **201.** « ou », circled, stands beside two possible matches of the roots. The choice is left on the sheet.
- **202.** « Il est possible même que mon départ … ait agi comme un catalyseur ». This conjecture concerns the mathematical milieu. On 208 the words « il se pourrait bien que la situation se renverse » similarly introduce a personal speculation.

## Slips

- **S197, scan 197, last generator list.** Written $t_{23},t_{24},t_{24}$. A possible intended last term is $t_{34}$. Both final subscripts visibly read 24. Among the six increasing pairs on 1 to 4, 34 alone is missing. Confidence is high for the repetition and medium for the proposed repair.
- **S196, scan 196, line 1.** « l'occurence » has two c's and one r. The apparent intended spelling is « l'occurrence ». Confidence is high after comparing the individual type impressions.
- **S17a–c, scans 198 and 204, last paragraph of L 17.** Both impressions have « personelle », « l'enquêté » and « asses stupéfiant ». The apparent intended forms are « personnelle », « l'enquête » and « assez stupéfiant ». The single n, the separate acute accent and the final s are visible on both scans. Confidence is high for the spellings and medium for the intended forms.
- **S205, scan 205, upper-right comparison.** The left side reads $b_a$, while the right side reads $t_{\bar a}$. Possibly $t_a$ was intended on the left, since the adjacent boxed edge generator is $t_a$. Confidence is low for the slip claim.

## Remarks of the model

- **M200 — my algebra check, high confidence.** With the substitution actually written on scan 200, collecting the coefficient of $\tau$ gives $\beta-\beta'$. Subtracting the two constant expressions on the last line gives $(\beta-\beta')\sigma$. Both residuals are zero under formal expansion.
- **M203 — my check of the dependence, high confidence for the transcribed equations.** In the last six rows of 203, each of the twelve individual indexed quantities occurs once per side when the equations are added. This gives the written $0=0$ and explains why any one row follows from the other five. One index in the second row is physically overwritten. The check uses the reading stated in the transcription.
- **M207 — my count, high confidence.** The five displayed counts on 207 give $4+4+6=14$ and $8+6=14$. The two groups of relations on 205 and 207 give $(4+4)+(12+12)=32$. These are counts of the displayed families. No independence test was made.
- **RQ196 — my reading question, medium confidence.** At the foot of 196 the final text has a cancelled doubtful b followed by doubtful « la » before « nature du travail créateur ». On revisiting the type, the initial also looks like the two humps of m, hence « ma ». This is a question about overlapping impressions. The final transcription was already fixed.
